articles.summary: Supports serial testing in the surveillance setting for patients with early-stage HCC Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that its Signatera molecular residual disease (MRD) test has received Medicare coverage through the Centers for Medicare Medicaid Services’ (CMS) Molecular Diagnostics Services Program (MolDX) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The coverage includes serial Signatera testing in the surveillance setting for patients with early-stage HCC who have no post-surgical evidence of disease. More than 42,000 new cases of liver cancer are expected in the U.S. in 2026 1 and HCC accounts for approximately 90% of primary liver cancers. 2 Even after curative-intent treatment (e.g., surgery), patients face a high risk of recurrence that makes post-treatment monitoring critical. 2 This Medicare coverage decision was supported by a real-world study of 125 patients with HCC published in JCO Precision Oncology . articles.summary: Solomon Moshkevich appointed Chief Executive Officer to lead the company's next phase of expansion Company separately reports third quarter 2026 financial results Natera, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that Solomon Moshkevich has been appointed Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors, effective immediately. Steve Chapman will step down from the CEO role and remain a consultant to the company for an extended period of time. Chapman will also remain an advisor to the Board of Directors. Moshkevich joined Natera in 2011. In his 15 years with the company, he has built and led multiple teams, including global marketing, product management, medical and scientific affairs, commercial operations, clinical trial operations, international sales and business development, regulatory and quality affairs, and portfolio strategy. articles.summary: New data at SITC includes real-world analysis highlighting that Signatera can inform immunotherapy duration and optimize treatment Natera, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced it will present important new Signatera data at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) Annual Meeting, taking place November 4–8 in Phoenix, Arizona. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed treatment for many metastatic cancers, and some patients achieve durable disease control. 1 However, it remains challenging for clinicians to determine how long to continue therapy, since imaging alone is prone to error and cannot show whether disease has cleared at the molecular level. 2,3 As a result, treatment duration remains an open question, particularly for patients who achieve a durable clinical response.
